paragraphs.text: The childhood-leukaemia pooled analyses report elevated estimates in higher residential magnetic-field categories. Those categories organize observational exposure histories. Their boundaries do not identify a biological point at which disease begins, and cannot be applied directly to a momentary meter reading.

An observational association also requires appraisal of bias, confounding, consistency and other evidence. It can be scientifically important without immediately becoming a compliance threshold. The same distinction prevents treating a regulatory reference level as a numerical personal cancer-risk calculator.

sections.title: Why an association does not define a new limit

sections.label: Biological response

paragraphs.text: The selected 5G experiment reports an EEG feature, while De Iuliis reports cellular changes in purified sperm. Both require their actual exposure and model. A measurable response is not automatically an injury, and its clinical meaning cannot be inferred solely from whether a headline says it occurred below a limit.

The appropriate questions are what changed, by how much, with what uncertainty, under which controls and whether the endpoint reflects an adverse outcome. Comparing experimental and compliance quantities must also respect averaging, geometry and biological system. The numerical relation alone does not complete the interpretation.

sections.title: A detected change requires its own interpretation

sections.label: Uncertainty

paragraphs.text: A correctly performed compliance comparison is useful evidence about the restrictions it evaluates. It should be reported accurately rather than dismissed as irrelevant. At the same time, a study of a proposed long-term outcome needs design-appropriate assessment rather than a declaration that it is impossible to discuss below a limit.

A precise statement identifies the exposure, the applicable assessment and the unresolved scientific question. It avoids a universal safe/unsafe label based on one number. When quantities or methods do not match, the honest next step is to resolve that comparison before drawing a health conclusion.

sections.title: How to avoid both overstatement and dismissal

sections.label: Multiple comparisons

paragraphs.text: A device can produce more than one field component or operate in several modes. A measurement made in one band cannot establish a result for the whole system if other relevant components were not assessed. The report should identify the frequency coverage and which restrictions were actually evaluated.

This is especially important when a consumer display gives one combined score or color. Its internal alarm setting may not represent the applicable document, averaging or population category. Ask for the physical quantity and method behind the display before treating the color as a compliance finding or a health conclusion.

sections.title: One measurement may require more than one assessment

takeaway: Being below an applicable limit is meaningful within that limit’s scope and measurement rules. It does not turn every chronic-outcome question into a directly tested result.
title: Does being below an exposure limit settle the health question?

faqs.q: Does industry funding prove a finding is false?

intro: Funding is part of evidence appraisal, alongside protocol control, methods, reporting and independent replication.

overview.text: Industry involvement can create conflicts of interest, but the scientifically useful question is how a sponsor could influence this particular study. Who chose the outcomes, held the data, decided the analysis and controlled publication? A funding acknowledgment alone may not answer those questions.

This page sets out an appraisal approach; it does not assign sponsor independence to papers whose disclosures have not been verified. Existing phone cohorts, case-control work and animal experiments still need their own design and source assessment. A reassuring or concerning result does not reveal its funding arrangements.

sections.label: Disclosure

paragraphs.text: Read the funding statement and conflict disclosures in the full article, including related corrections or supplements. Separate institutional support, equipment provision, investigator interests and direct project funding. Then look for explicit statements about the sponsor’s role in design, data collection, analysis, writing and the decision to publish.

Absence of a reported role is not proof that no role existed. Equally, receiving support does not establish that a result was manipulated. Record what is disclosed, what is missing and what consequences those gaps have for appraisal, rather than filling missing information with assumptions.

sections.title: Distinguish who paid from who controlled the work

sections.label: Methods

paragraphs.text: Potential influence becomes more assessable when connected to choices: a weak exposure contrast, short follow-up, a favorable comparator, selective outcomes or an analysis chosen after results were seen. The same weaknesses can occur without industry support. They need examination regardless of the sponsor.

For example, the phone studies already have identifiable questions about recalled versus prospective exposure, rare tumours and follow-up. Those limitations should be evaluated on their own merits. They cannot be repaired by a nonindustry funding label or dismissed solely by an industry one.

sections.title: Trace the possible influence to a concrete decision

sections.label: Robustness

paragraphs.text: Prespecified protocols, transparent analysis decisions and sensitivity analyses can make selective interpretation easier to detect. A useful question is whether the conclusion changes when plausible exposure errors, alternative adjustment choices or influential subgroups are considered. The actual analyses and their limitations need to be read.

Independent replication is strongest when it uses different participants, investigators and measurement approaches. Multiple publications from one programme may provide detail without constituting independent confirmation. The overlapping childhood-leukaemia pooled analyses illustrate why family reconciliation matters before a review counts agreement.

sections.title: Ask whether the conclusion survives reasonable alternatives

sections.label: Reader judgment

paragraphs.text: A good evidence table can display funding and sponsor-role information separately from effect magnitude and certainty. A verified conflict should be visible; an unverified statement should remain unknown. That distinction allows readers to inspect the evidence without treating funding as either irrelevant or an automatic verdict.

The current selected-source collection does not supply a completed funding-bias analysis across the whole EMF literature. Its practical standard is to verify disclosures, identify plausible influence, inspect methods and compare independent evidence. Scientific appraisal remains pending where those steps have not been completed; no sponsor-based grade is invented.

sections.title: Keep conflict assessment proportional and explicit

sections.label: Literature selection

paragraphs.text: A review can be influenced through which studies it searches for, includes, excludes or emphasizes. Funding assessment should therefore cover the synthesis as well as individual papers. A transparent search, explicit eligibility criteria and a recorded treatment of conflicting results make those choices easier to inspect.

A sponsor-independent review can still select evidence poorly, and a disclosed conflict does not tell the reader which result will survive reanalysis. The decisive work is to trace the conclusion to the included evidence and test whether reasonable changes alter it. Disclosure, methods and interpretation should remain visible together.

sections.title: Appraisal also applies to the review process

takeaway: A sponsor’s name is a reason to inspect influence, not a substitute for assessing the study. Funding and control should be verified rather than inferred from the direction of a result.

intro: Start with the source and physical quantity, then ask what outcome was studied.

overview.text: An electromagnetic-field question becomes easier when it is made concrete: a mobile phone beside the head, a power-frequency magnetic field in a home, an induction cooker or the static component of an MRI system. Those sources cannot be treated as one exposure merely because they share the abbreviation EMF.

A complete health claim also identifies the outcome. Tumour diagnoses, a sleep EEG feature, a semen measurement and DNA fragmentation in isolated cells are different endpoints. The selected studies illustrate these distinctions; they do not form a universal safety score for every source and disease.

sections.label: Field types

paragraphs.text: Frequency describes how a time-varying field changes. Electrical power systems commonly involve 50 or 60 Hz fields, while wireless communication uses radiofrequency fields. Static fields require separate handling because they do not oscillate in the same way. These differences affect which physical interactions and measurement methods are relevant.

A mixed system can contain several components. Identifying only a device’s familiar name may hide that mixture. For a reader, the useful first step is to name the component being discussed rather than import a result from whichever EMF paper is easiest to find.

sections.title: Frequency tells you what kind of question to ask

sections.label: Exposure and dose

paragraphs.text: An external field reading describes conditions at a location. Absorbed dose depends on how that field couples to a body or tissue. SAR expresses absorbed power per mass, while magnetic flux density and electric-field strength describe other quantities. They should be compared only within an appropriate exposure model.

Use duration and distance also need context. A phone held to the ear, a far-field exposure and a household magnetic field do not share one universal distance formula. A study should describe the source, geometry, operating state, averaging and relevant body region before its numbers are used elsewhere.

sections.title: A source label is not the absorbed quantity

sections.label: Biological endpoints

paragraphs.text: The selected sleep experiment found a genotype-specific EEG feature; the sperm-cell experiment reported cellular changes in an isolated preparation. Neither observation is a diagnosis of disease in a person using a device. Their biological meaning should be investigated without expanding the endpoint beyond what was measured.

The same discipline applies in the other direction. A cohort without an observed tumour increase is informative about those diagnoses and exposure measures, but does not directly measure every biological pathway. A good explanation preserves both the actual finding and the questions it was not designed to answer.

sections.title: A response is not automatically an adverse outcome

sections.label: Hazard and risk

paragraphs.text: IARC’s 2011 RF classification is a hazard assessment, with limited evidence described for glioma and acoustic neuroma. It does not provide the probability of disease for an individual phone user. Its date and remit should remain visible beside later primary studies.

A personal risk estimate would require a suitable exposure-to-outcome model and a relevant baseline risk. The selected animal experiments and human observational studies do not authorize a calculation from one meter reading or a number of calls. Understanding the evidence means asking which comparison is actually supported.

sections.title: Why classifications and personal predictions differ

sections.label: Reading a claim

paragraphs.text: Identify the source and field component, the population or experimental model, the dose or exposure proxy, the comparator and the measured outcome. Then examine timing and uncertainty. These details distinguish a direct answer from background context and prevent a paper about one source from being presented as proof about another.

The website’s exposure and outcome directories offer the two useful starting points: what produces the field, or what health question concerns you. Follow their matched comparisons to the underlying study records. Keep selected-source coverage and pending scientific appraisal visible instead of interpreting a populated page as a completed systematic review.

takeaway: “EMF” covers different fields and exposure situations. Frequency, dose, body region, timing and endpoint determine whether evidence applies.

intro: Units and averaging describe different physical quantities; the useful comparison is a matched one.

overview.text: An exposure number is only as interpretable as the quantity behind it. Electric-field strength, magnetic flux density, power density and absorbed power per mass describe different aspects of exposure. A comparison can be wrong even when both numbers are measured accurately, if they represent different things.

The same applies to research. Reported call time in a phone cohort, a modeled brain dose and a residential magnetic-field category are different exposure descriptions. None can be replaced automatically by a spot reading from a consumer meter.

sections.label: Units

paragraphs.text: Magnetic flux density may be expressed in tesla or its smaller units; electric-field strength uses volts per metre. RF assessments may use power density or SAR, the absorbed power per mass. A unit conversion within the same quantity does not create a general conversion between different kinds of field.

For example, converting microtesla to milligauss changes the unit scale, while converting a household magnetic-field value to a phone SAR would require a physical model and relevant assumptions. The presence of familiar numbers on one display should not imply that all its modes measure an interchangeable dose.

sections.title: Keep the quantity attached to the number

sections.label: Instrument match

paragraphs.text: An assessment should document frequency range, response to the signal, calibration, sensitivity, saturation and uncertainty. A power-frequency instrument cannot be assumed to characterize Wi-Fi. For a mixed environment, the required components and the limitations of each measurement need to be identified.

FOPH’s WLAN guidance specifically cautions that measuring wireless emissions requires more complex techniques than ordinary commercially available handheld equipment provides. That source-specific limitation is important when an online demonstration treats a brief display reading as a complete WLAN assessment.

sections.title: A meter must fit the field and question

sections.label: Averaging

paragraphs.text: A peak can describe a short event; a time average describes a chosen interval; a spatial average describes a defined region. A guideline comparison must use the relevant rule. A research category may represent another duration again, such as a residential exposure estimate rather than an instantaneous device reading.

Record device activity, electrical load, room location, probe placement and measurement duration. Repeated observations can reveal variation, but do not automatically reconstruct past exposure. A carefully measured present-day home is still not the same thing as a person’s exposure history across many years.

sections.title: Peak, local and long-term values are not the same

sections.label: Comparability

paragraphs.text: Draper used birth-address distance from power lines as a proxy; the pooled leukaemia analyses used other residential exposure descriptions. Their results cannot be converted into a universal safe distance or applied to a phone’s RF measurement. Keep the study’s actual exposure metric visible.

HERMES used modeled brain dose and COSMOS used phone-use information. These examples show why exposure assessment is part of causal interpretation, not a box ticked once a number exists. Ask how well the measure captures the biologically relevant source, tissue and period.

sections.title: Match the measurement to the evidence

sections.label: Interpreting results

paragraphs.text: The first conclusion is physical: what quantity was present, where and under which conditions? The second is whether an appropriate assessment matches the applicable restriction. The third concerns health evidence about a specified endpoint. Those judgments are connected but require different information.

A report should state where the evidence stops. It may characterize a source well while offering no individual disease prediction. For a complex workplace, suspected electrical fault or a formal compliance question, use the relevant qualified assessment rather than treating a consumer alarm setting as a diagnosis or legal conclusion.

sections.title: Separate description, compliance and health inference

takeaway: A meaningful measurement needs the field type, frequency range, unit, location, operating conditions and averaging period. A meter reading is not a health diagnosis.

faqs.q: Does “not significant” mean no effect?

faqs.q: Does a relative increase tell me my absolute risk?

faqs.a: No. Bias, confounding, study design and outcome relevance still need assessment.
faqs.q: Is statistical significance proof that RF caused the outcome?

intro: Read effect size, baseline risk, uncertainty and study design together.

overview.text: A risk headline often compresses several different quantities into a phrase such as “increases risk.” To interpret it, find the outcome, the comparison groups, the time period, the estimate and its uncertainty. Then ask whether the design supports a causal interpretation. The number alone cannot supply that answer.

The EMF collection includes cohort estimates, case-control odds, pooled analyses and test-score changes. Their scales are different. COSMOS and INTERPHONE address tumours through different designs; HERMES reports memory-score change. Their numerical results should not be placed on one undifferentiated risk scale.

sections.label: Relative and absolute

paragraphs.text: As a purely hypothetical teaching example, an outcome occurring in two people per thousand compared with one per thousand represents a doubling in relative terms and one additional event per thousand in absolute terms. These are invented example values, not an EMF study result or a personal prediction.

An actual absolute-risk statement needs the relevant baseline population and time horizon, as well as an estimate that can legitimately be applied to it. A case-control odds ratio cannot simply be multiplied into an arbitrary lifetime risk. If those inputs are absent, the correct response is to leave the absolute effect unspecified.

sections.title: The baseline changes what a relative effect means

sections.label: Estimate type

paragraphs.text: A risk ratio compares risks over a defined period; odds compare the chance of an event with the chance of its absence; hazard models concern event rates over follow-up. The selected records illustrate why a label matters: INTERPHONE reports odds from a case-control design, while cohort analyses use follow-up information.

The Million Women Study record preserves a reporting nuance: the authors describe relative risks while the methods specify Cox hazard ratios. A careful summary retains the source’s actual method instead of smoothing every estimate into an identical statistic. These distinctions become especially important when attempting an absolute-risk translation.

sections.title: Risk ratios, odds and hazards have different meanings

sections.label: Uncertainty

paragraphs.text: A confidence interval expresses uncertainty under the analysis’s assumptions. A wide interval means several effect sizes remain compatible with the data and model. Including no difference does not establish that the true effect is exactly zero; excluding it does not show that bias or confounding is absent.

HERMES is a useful example: its full-sample interval included no difference, while selected analyses suggested an association. Both belong in the account. The uncertainty concerns a particular figural-memory score and modeled dose, not a general estimate of brain injury.

sections.title: Read the interval with the estimate

sections.label: Importance and cause

paragraphs.text: Statistical significance does not indicate whether a change is clinically meaningful, whether the exposure caused it, or whether it applies to a reader’s situation. The selected sleep experiment measured a genotype-specific EEG feature. Its clinical significance requires evidence beyond detecting a difference in that feature.

Likewise, INTERPHONE’s high-use estimate requires its recall and participation limits. The pooled leukaemia estimates require selection and confounding assessment. A numerical association remains valuable evidence, but a causal conclusion needs an account of alternative explanations and consistency across relevant designs.

sections.title: A detectable difference can still be hard to interpret

sections.label: A reading checklist

paragraphs.text: Ask who was included, how many relevant events occurred, which group was the reference, what duration was covered and whether the analysis was planned. For a subgroup, check the full-sample result and the number of comparisons. For a pooled estimate, check whether its reports overlap.

Finally, state the result in the study’s own scope: a tumour subtype, semen measure, memory test or EEG feature under a defined exposure comparison. A useful summary can be concise without discarding uncertainty. It should leave unsupported conversions and individual predictions blank rather than filling them with an apparently precise number.

sections.title: Keep the denominator and comparison in view

takeaway: A relative estimate does not state the absolute chance of disease. An interval crossing no difference is not proof of equality, and statistical significance does not establish causation.
title: Reading risk numbers without being misled

faqs.q: Does randomization make a study relevant to every question?

faqs.a: Not necessarily. They often reuse earlier data and may overlap with one another.
faqs.q: Are pooled analyses new independent populations?

faqs.a: No. A human-derived cell preparation is still a different biological model from an intact person.
faqs.q: Are cell experiments human health trials?

intro: Choose the design that can answer the exposure, outcome and timescale of the question.

overview.text: A study is useful when its design matches the question. A rare tumour may require an observational design; an immediate symptom trigger can be tested with real and sham exposure; a controlled lifetime animal experiment addresses hazard under a specified protocol. Calling one design universally best hides these differences.

The selected public collection contains examples of each. They can teach the structure of evidence without making the collection a completed systematic review. Begin with the comparison a study creates, then examine measurement, bias, precision and applicability before interpreting its result.

sections.label: Cohorts

paragraphs.text: Cohorts describe exposure before the incident outcomes being analyzed. COSMOS and the Million Women Study contribute this kind of phone-and-brain-tumour evidence. Their sequence reduces some reliance on recalling use after a diagnosis, but does not automatically produce a precise measure of dose.

Changing use, confounding, loss to follow-up, latency and rare outcomes remain relevant. A large enrolled population can still produce limited information about a very rare subtype or an uncommon exposure pattern. Read the events and exposure contrast rather than judging the study only by its headline sample size.

sections.title: Follow exposure information toward later outcomes

sections.label: Case-control studies

paragraphs.text: Case-control studies compare people with an outcome and controls, then examine earlier exposure. They can study rare tumours efficiently. INTERPHONE and MOBI-Kids provide examples, with recalled use or exposure reconstruction and participation among the important appraisal questions.

The controls need to represent the exposure distribution that would have occurred in the population giving rise to the cases. Differential participation or recall can distort the comparison. An observed odds ratio is therefore a result to interpret with the design, not an automatic causal risk ratio for every user.

sections.title: Work backward from an uncommon diagnosis

sections.label: Sham trials

paragraphs.text: In a sham-controlled exposure experiment, the aim is to change the signal while keeping other circumstances comparable. Blinding can reduce the influence of knowing the condition on symptom reports. The headache and base-station experiments use this approach for specific acute questions.

Their results are limited by sample, tested signal, duration and endpoint. A trial of short-term discomfort cannot settle a decades-long tumour question. The sleep experiment is controlled too, but its EEG endpoint is distinct from a clinical sleep disorder. Matching the question remains essential even with randomization.

sections.title: Test a defined short-term signal comparison

sections.label: Animal and cell work

paragraphs.text: Animal experiments can control exposure and examine disease over a substantial part of the lifespan. Cell experiments can investigate particular mechanisms. NTP and Ramazzini concern rat tumours; De Iuliis concerns purified human sperm outside the body. Those are valuable but different models.

Translation to people requires species or tissue relevance, dosimetry, temperature and schedule to be assessed. A controlled result does not erase the model mismatch. An isolated-cell response is not a clinical infertility outcome, and an animal tumour count does not supply an individual phone-use risk.

sections.title: Control exposure while changing the biological model

sections.label: Pooled evidence

paragraphs.text: Pooled analyses can improve precision by combining participant data or results, but inherit important strengths and weaknesses from their inputs. The Ahlbom and Greenland leukaemia analyses overlap in underlying studies. They are not two new independent cohorts.

A synthesis should reconcile report families, align exposures and outcomes, explain why studies differ and preserve missing information. Reviews, engineering reports and official guidance have useful roles too, but they should be identified as such rather than counted as new primary clinical experiments.

sections.title: Combine compatible evidence without counting it twice

takeaway: No study design answers every EMF question. Cohorts, case-control studies, sham trials and animal experiments contribute different evidence and have different limitations.

intro: Translate a controlled animal finding through exposure, biology and outcome rather than a simple dose ratio.

overview.text: Animal studies are important because they can control conditions that cannot easily be assigned in people. That strength does not make the animals a miniature version of every human exposure. A useful translation asks which biological process is being tested and whether the relevant tissue and dose are comparable.

NTP and Ramazzini illustrate the issue through long-term rat tumour experiments. Their male-rat heart schwannoma findings belong in the evidence, while their whole-body exposure, schedule and species constrain a human interpretation. The purpose of translation is to make that reasoning explicit, neither to dismiss the model nor to skip directly to a personal risk.

sections.label: Model relevance

paragraphs.text: A model is relevant when it can inform the biological question being asked. The tissue, age, sex and disease process matter. A result in one sex or organ should remain attached to those details rather than becoming a claim about all animals, all cancers or all human users.

In the selected NTP record, evidence judgments differ by sex and tumour, with the clearest statement concerning malignant heart schwannomas in male rats. Ramazzini’s statistically significant heart finding also concerns male rats at the highest exposure. Those specifics define the starting observation to be translated.

sections.title: Start with the reason for using that species

sections.label: Dose and geometry

paragraphs.text: External field strength, whole-body absorbed power and localized tissue exposure describe different aspects of a protocol. A person making a call and a rat in a whole-body exposure system do not receive interchangeable distributions simply because the signal names overlap. A translation needs dosimetry appropriate to the relevant tissues.

Exposure duration and schedule also matter. A brief daily use pattern cannot be represented by a lifetime schedule without an explicit model, and a lower external intensity does not on its own settle biological equivalence. Avoid a direct multiplication or division that turns a dose comparison into an unvalidated risk equation.

sections.title: Compare absorbed exposure rather than labels

sections.label: Study interpretation

paragraphs.text: Check allocation, sham or control conditions, animal numbers, pathology procedures, survival and the pattern across dose groups. Those features affect whether an apparent tumour difference is robust within the experiment before any cross-species claim is considered. Small tumour counts and survival differences are material limitations in the selected records.

Replication should mean more than another paper using the word RF. The relevant question is whether an independent study tests a sufficiently comparable exposure and biological endpoint, with differences explained. A shared tumour signal across different protocols can be informative while still requiring careful assessment of those differences.

sections.title: Appraise the animal result before extrapolating it

sections.label: Human evidence

paragraphs.text: Human cohorts examine diagnosed outcomes under actual but imperfectly measured use patterns. The selected phone cohorts did not show increased brain-tumour incidence; INTERPHONE’s high-use glioma association retains recall and selection concerns. These results need to be considered alongside, rather than substituted for, the animal findings.

A credible synthesis explains what each evidence stream supports and what remains uncertain between them. The rat experiments do not establish a numerical risk for a phone user, and the human cohorts do not make the animal pathology irrelevant. Their combination is an appraisal task that remains distinct from simply having retrieved the reports.

sections.title: Use translation as one part of a combined explanation

sections.label: Cells and mechanisms

paragraphs.text: The same translation discipline applies to cell work. De Iuliis studied purified sperm exposed outside the body, with cellular endpoints and a later correction. Calling the cells human does not make the preparation an intact-person fertility experiment.

Mechanistic observations can suggest a pathway worth testing, but a pathway claim needs evidence that the steps occur under relevant exposure conditions and lead to the proposed adverse outcome. A cellular assay, a physiological feature and clinical disease remain different levels of inference even when they appear in the same narrative.

sections.title: A human-derived sample is still a model

takeaway: Animal findings can identify hazards and test mechanisms. Applying them to human health requires a justified link across species, tissues, dose and exposure schedule.

intro: Identify the issuing body, document edition, exposure scenario and measurement rules before using a limit.

overview.text: An exposure limit is not just a number in a table. It belongs to an assessment framework with a frequency range, population category, body region, averaging rules and rationale. The site links ICNIRP RF and low-frequency context, while recognizing that a guideline is not automatically the law in every country.

Agency statements also serve different purposes. IARC’s 2011 RF assessment concerns carcinogenic hazard; FDA’s cell-phone hub explains shared US regulatory roles with the FCC. Neither should be flattened into an unnamed global consensus or treated as a substitute for reading a specific applicable standard.

sections.label: Document roles

paragraphs.text: A scientific body can recommend exposure restrictions; a regulator can adopt requirements or use another instrument; a hazard agency can assess evidence about cancer. Those outputs may inform one another without answering the same question. Always state which body made the statement and what its remit was.

For example, the linked FDA hub describes the FCC setting US cell-phone RF emission limits while FDA supplies scientific expertise and information. That is jurisdiction-specific institutional context. It is not a legal analysis of a European workplace, a home measurement or a different medical system.

sections.title: Separate advice, assessment and legal adoption

sections.label: Edition and range

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP’s 2020 RF publication specifies its frequency scope and replaces identified portions of earlier guidance. The low-frequency context addresses a different range and interactions. A citation to “ICNIRP limits” without a document and edition can therefore leave the relevant rule unresolved.

A mixed exposure may require several component assessments rather than one chosen value. Before comparing numbers, establish whether the quantity is external field strength, absorbed power, induced field or another metric, and whether the reference level or basic restriction is the relevant part of the framework.

sections.title: Use the frequency and version that apply

sections.label: Measurement rules

paragraphs.text: Body region, spatial average, time average and exposure category affect interpretation. A short peak, a whole-body average and a localized measurement cannot be compared casually with a single published number. The measurement method needs to produce a quantity compatible with the restriction being evaluated.

A pass or exceedance statement should preserve uncertainty, operating conditions and any required assessment steps. An apparent mismatch with a reference level may call for a more detailed assessment under the framework; it should not be translated automatically into a diagnosis of injury. Formal compliance belongs with the appropriate qualified process.

sections.title: The test conditions are part of the limit

sections.label: Health evidence

paragraphs.text: The residential magnetic-field categories in the childhood-leukaemia analyses are epidemiological groups. Their boundaries are not experimental thresholds or regulatory limits. The observed association and its causal uncertainty need their own explanation, independent of a meter’s alarm setting.

Likewise, a response in a cell or EEG study requires outcome-specific interpretation. The fact that a result is described relative to a limit does not itself establish clinical harm, replication or everyday applicability. Standards context and primary health evidence should appear together with their roles clearly labeled.

sections.title: Keep chronic associations and acute restrictions distinct

sections.label: Using this guide

paragraphs.text: Request the jurisdiction, exact instrument or standard, edition, source and frequency components, population category, operating scenario and the assessment method. Then establish who is qualified to interpret it. Those inputs are needed before a particular product, workplace or property can be evaluated.

This selected-source guide explains how to read such an assessment; it does not issue a legal compliance certificate or a universal safe-distance rule. Its citations retain their dates and scope, and a newer document should trigger a checked update rather than a silent substitution that changes the meaning of an earlier comparison.

takeaway: Guidelines, hazard assessments and legally adopted requirements have different roles. A correct comparison needs the actual document and its applicable physical quantity.

intro: A useful home assessment starts with a source map and a defined measurement question.

overview.text: A home contains several potential field sources, including wiring and appliances, wireless devices and contributions from outside. A useful survey asks which component and time period matter to the concern. Searching every room for the largest display number without a defined quantity can create a misleading picture.

The practical goal can be modest and concrete: characterize a source during ordinary and relevant higher-use conditions, document variation, and explain what can and cannot be compared with research or guidance. That is different from producing an individual health-risk score from the survey.

sections.label: Source map

paragraphs.text: Separate power-frequency electric and magnetic fields from radiofrequency sources. Note the room, occupied position and operating activity. A router, a phone, an induction hob and household wiring do not need the same measurement method. A mixed device or setting may require more than one component assessment.

Define the question before changing anything. Is the concern an appliance during use, an overnight position, a possible wiring issue or a formal limit comparison? A clear question determines which sources, locations and durations deserve measurement and makes the resulting report easier to interpret.

sections.title: List what is operating and where people spend time

sections.label: Variation

paragraphs.text: Record instrument range, calibration, probe placement, orientation, time and electrical or data load. Repeat relevant conditions where needed. A brief maximum beside a source and a typical occupied-position average describe different scenarios; neither should be presented as the other.

The WLAN fact sheet explains traffic-related variation and cautions about ordinary handheld equipment for wireless-emission assessment. The mobile-phone fact sheet describes connection-dependent transmission. These examples show why source operation and instrument suitability belong in a home report.

sections.title: Measure the circumstances rather than one unexplained maximum

sections.label: Research comparison

paragraphs.text: The childhood-leukaemia studies used residential exposure descriptions and pooled observational comparisons, while Draper used birth-address distance. A current home measurement cannot reconstruct those histories or turn their category boundaries into personal disease thresholds.

The same issue arises with phone cohorts, which use reported or calibrated use measures. An RF reading beside a device is not automatically the exposure metric used in a cancer analysis. Match source, quantity and time window before drawing an evidence-based comparison.

sections.title: A room reading does not reproduce a cohort exposure history

sections.label: Practical changes

paragraphs.text: An optional change in placement, operating schedule or radio settings can be assessed as a physical intervention. Record the starting condition and keep other relevant conditions comparable. A measured reduction under that arrangement is more informative than an unverified promise that a room has been made EMF-free.

FOPH provides optional WLAN exposure-reduction suggestions, but those are not a clinical trial of a home intervention. If sleep or symptoms also change, separate the observation from a claim that RF caused the difference. Alerts, routines, noise or expectations may have changed at the same time.

sections.title: Document what the change actually changes

sections.label: Assessment report

paragraphs.text: A suspected electrical fault, an implant-related concern or a formal compliance assessment needs the relevant professional and source-specific information. A consumer meter or a phone application should not be used to certify wiring safety or diagnose a medical cause. The report should state its scope rather than imply those services.

A useful written result includes the question, instrument and limits, source conditions, locations, duration, uncertainty, photographs or diagrams where helpful, and the specific comparison used. It should also state unresolved questions. Good documentation makes a later remeasurement or expert review possible without inventing certainty from one visit.

takeaway: Identify the field components, source activity and occupied locations. Household readings describe physical conditions; they do not independently predict illness.

intro: Start with the family’s actual decision, then separate age-specific evidence, exposure changes and proven health benefits.

overview.text: Family questions often concern several sources at once: a child’s phone, a bedroom router, a baby monitor, a cooker or the location of a home. A useful discussion begins with the decision and the relevant age, rather than a blanket verdict on all EMF. An exposure choice can be reasonable without being presented as a proven medical intervention.

The selected childhood evidence is also varied. MOBI-Kids concerns brain tumours and wireless-phone use in young people, HERMES concerns adolescent memory and modeled RF dose, and the leukaemia pooled analyses concern residential power-frequency magnetic fields. Those tracks should remain distinct whenever families read across pages.

sections.label: Child-specific evidence

paragraphs.text: MOBI-Kids found no evidence of a causal association in the young people and tumour comparison studied, while acknowledging bias and exposure error. HERMES reported a memory association with a full-sample interval including no difference and more suggestive selected analyses. Neither is a lifetime study of all childhood devices.

Adult cohorts remain useful context, but their populations and exposure measures stay attached. The Million Women Study cannot directly answer every early-life question. Recognizing that mismatch allows adult evidence to inform a discussion without becoming an unlimited child-specific reassurance.

sections.title: Match age, use pattern and outcome

sections.label: Bedroom choices

paragraphs.text: A decision to move a phone or change alerts can affect behavior, convenience and the exposure arrangement at the same time. A change in sleep after several adjustments does not identify RF as the cause. The selected 5G EEG experiment concerns a narrower controlled physiological comparison.

For Wi-Fi, the FOPH fact sheet provides optional exposure-reduction suggestions and describes traffic-dependent emissions. It is useful source context, rather than a trial showing a sleep benefit from nightly switching. A family’s preference should not be packaged as a clinically proven rule.

sections.title: Separate signals from device routines

sections.label: Baby monitors

paragraphs.text: FOPH distinguishes audio/video monitors, network cameras and phone-based arrangements. Its March 2026 fact sheet covers ordinary audio/video monitoring rather than advanced bodily-function monitoring. Device type and transmission behavior therefore need to be identified before comparing exposure or interpreting a claim.

The same fact sheet emphasizes checking connection and voice-activation operation. Any placement or radio-setting choice should preserve the device’s intended monitoring function and follow its instructions. A claimed RF reduction is not a reason to assume that a disabled link, missed alert or more distant parent is an equivalent arrangement.

sections.title: Function and placement belong in the same decision

sections.label: Different sources

paragraphs.text: The residential leukaemia association concerns power-frequency magnetic fields, not a general result about Wi-Fi. An induction hob is another source with its own field geometry and operating conditions. FOPH’s cooker context emphasizes cookware placement and use instructions, and advises implant users to obtain relevant medical advice.

These distinctions prevent one dramatic study from driving unrelated changes across the home. Where a source-specific outcome assessment is incomplete, explain that gap and the available context. Do not infer a pregnancy, infant or implant conclusion solely from an adult phone or animal experiment.

sections.title: Keep household questions on their own evidence tracks

sections.label: Proportional choices

paragraphs.text: A family may prioritize convenience, sleep routines, communication, cost or a preferred exposure arrangement. Those are legitimate decision factors, but a claim of disease prevention requires matched health evidence. Avoid expensive products justified only by a meter display, testimonials or a biological surrogate.

For persistent symptoms, fertility concerns or an implanted device, use the relevant qualified clinical guidance. This website helps identify the exposure and evidence question; it cannot choose a diagnosis or replace device-specific instructions. The most useful family plan is one whose purpose and evidence are both clear.

sections.title: Ask what benefit has actually been demonstrated

takeaway: Children’s brain-tumour, memory and residential magnetic-field studies answer different questions. Practical device choices should retain that distinction and preserve their ordinary safety functions.

intro: Symptoms deserve care even when a proposed environmental cause has not been established.

overview.text: People use “electromagnetic hypersensitivity” to describe symptoms they attribute to fields or devices. Experiencing symptoms and identifying their cause are different questions. A useful approach takes the experience seriously while examining possible triggers with methods that can distinguish exposure from accompanying circumstances.

The WHO’s December 2005 backgrounder describes the symptoms as real and potentially disabling, while not establishing an EMF cause. The selected Eltiti and headache experiments contribute more specific blinded comparisons. These sources are dated and scoped; they should not be represented as an individual diagnostic test or a completed current treatment guideline.

sections.label: Clinical question

paragraphs.text: A useful account includes the symptom, timing, duration, severity and effect on sleep, work or daily activities. That description can support a clinical conversation without presuming a single cause. A symptom label based on attribution does not identify which biological process is responsible.

WHO’s backgrounder recommends assessment of medical and psychological contributors and relevant environmental factors, with attention to functioning. That is a broad assessment approach rather than a claim that every person has the same explanation. An appropriate clinician can investigate the individual’s symptoms and circumstances.

sections.title: Describe what happens and how it affects life

sections.label: Exposure attribution

paragraphs.text: Knowing or believing a signal is present can accompany changes in symptom reports, making unblinded before-and-after observations difficult to interpret. A sham comparison attempts to hold circumstances similar while concealing which exposure is active. It tests a specified proposed trigger rather than whether symptoms exist.

Eltiti’s blinded results did not show the tested base-station-like signals increasing symptom number or severity. The selected headache experiment found no significant difference in pain and discomfort between real and sham exposure. Their samples, signals and acute durations remain important limits.

sections.title: What a blinded test is designed to separate

sections.label: Meaning of a result

paragraphs.text: A negative acute test does not settle every chronic disease or exposure situation. Conversely, symptoms during a known exposure do not establish that RF caused them. A fair interpretation says which immediate comparison was tested, which outcomes were recorded and what uncertainty remains.

Expectation-related contributions are compatible with real symptoms; they are not an accusation of invention. But these studies also do not diagnose expectation as the cause in every participant. The individual’s clinical assessment and the experimental group result serve different purposes.

sections.title: Avoid two overextensions of provocation evidence

sections.label: Environment and routines

paragraphs.text: Turning off devices can also change light, alerts, noise, posture, activity or worry. If several circumstances change and someone feels better, the observation may still be useful, but it does not isolate RF. A practical record should describe those accompanying changes rather than assign one mechanism from timing alone.

WHO’s historical backgrounder specifically discusses workstation, lighting, air-quality and stress-related contributors as matters for assessment. It should be read as contextual guidance, not a predetermined explanation for a particular person. The goal is to identify addressable problems while keeping causal claims testable.

sections.title: Look at factors that change together

sections.label: Support and claims

paragraphs.text: A claim that an accessory treats symptoms needs an appropriate clinical comparison, not just a lower field reading. Outcomes should include symptom burden, daily function and adverse effects, with a credible comparator and attention to expectations. This collection does not establish a product-based treatment.

Support can focus on the person’s needs while uncertainty about cause remains. Persistent or disabling symptoms warrant appropriate professional assessment. Research summaries can inform that conversation, but neither a website label nor a meter alarm can determine the diagnosis or justify a promise of cure.

sections.title: Judge interventions by symptoms and functioning

takeaway: Blinded studies did not support the tested RF exposures as immediate symptom triggers. That finding does not dismiss symptoms or supply an individual diagnosis; assessment should address the person’s clinical and functional needs.

intro: Follow each claim from the exposure–outcome comparison to the actual source and its review status.

overview.text: The evidence product begins with a specific comparison: a source and field component, a population or model, an exposure or dose, a comparator, an outcome and a time window. This prevents a paper about one narrow setting from silently answering a broader parent page. The same comparison can appear from either its exposure or outcome route.

This edition is based on selected sources and clearly marked editorial interpretation. It is not a claim to have completed an exhaustive systematic review of every EMF question. Source-reading status and unresolved scientific appraisal remain visible, while effect descriptions retain the actual endpoint and decisive limitations.

sections.label: Source basis

paragraphs.text: A title and identifier establish a report’s identity, not its methods or result. An abstract supports a narrower reading than a verified full text with tables and supplements. The public study records distinguish their source basis, so a reader can see when a summary rests on an abstract rather than a complete appraisal.

The distinction matters in this collection. Some phone and animal records retain abstract-based status; others, such as the Million Women and Eltiti records, have a full-text reading basis. Neither label alone establishes risk of bias or certainty, and neither should be upgraded because the page has been expanded.

sections.title: Separate metadata, abstract and full-text knowledge

sections.label: Fidelity and appraisal

paragraphs.text: Source-fidelity checking asks whether a statement, number, unit, population and limitation match the original passage or table. Appraisal asks whether the design and conduct support the inference. A quotation can be accurately transcribed from a weak comparison; an otherwise valuable study can also be summarized incorrectly.

The selected INTERPHONE and HERMES records show why both matter. Their subgroup findings need the full comparison and uncertainty, while their exposure and bias limitations need scientific interpretation. Displaying the interesting estimate accurately is necessary, but does not complete the causal assessment.

sections.title: Check what was reported before judging how persuasive it is

sections.label: Evidence judgment

paragraphs.text: A large estimate can have low precision or substantial bias, while a small estimate can be measured more reliably. Direction, magnitude, clinical importance and certainty should therefore not be collapsed into one favorable or unfavorable badge. A biological endpoint also needs its own relevance to an adverse clinical outcome.

The 5G sleep finding concerns a physiological feature; the sperm-cell finding concerns an isolated preparation. Neither receives a clinical disease grade merely because a change was reported. An editorial assessment must explain applicability and missing inputs rather than invent a certainty category when appraisal is incomplete.

sections.title: Keep effect size separate from certainty

sections.label: Identity and updates

paragraphs.text: Reports need stable identities and a study-family map. Pooled analyses can reuse participants, so publication count is not independent evidence count. The leukaemia pooled analyses retain that overlap explicitly rather than appearing as two new cohorts.

A correction or concern belongs to its matched article, not every paper that cites it. The De Iuliis correction stays linked to the original figure and replication description. If a material source changes, dependent summaries should be checked and their update history should say what changed and why.

sections.title: Treat corrections and overlapping reports precisely

sections.label: Reading status

paragraphs.text: An editorial draft can explain the source, findings and uncertainty while scientific review remains pending. It should not display invented clinician approval, a completed systematic-review claim or an unsupported individual risk calculation. Missing evidence means incomplete assessment rather than proof of no effect.

Use the bibliography to reach original sources, the research feed to inspect study records and the exposure/outcome pages to see the comparison’s scope. When a result seems stronger than its source basis, the useful question is which statement, endpoint or limitation needs correction. This makes the site auditable without disguising open work as a finished grade.

sections.title: Know what an editorial draft permits you to conclude

takeaway: Effect magnitude, source verification, evidence certainty and human scientific approval are separate. A populated page or retrieved full text does not establish that all four have been completed.

intro: A methods companion for comparing NTP and Ramazzini without treating their exposure systems as interchangeable.

overview.text: A long-term RF animal experiment is a system of exposure generation, dosimetry, animal allocation, follow-up and pathology. The methods determine what comparison its tumour findings can support. Reading only the title or a single field-strength value loses the information needed to compare programmes.

NTP’s selected record concerns whole-body 900 MHz GSM/CDMA exposure in rats. Ramazzini’s concerns far-field 1.8 GHz GSM exposure from prenatal life to natural death. Both contribute to hazard assessment, but the frequency, exposure arrangement and schedule need to be documented separately before findings are synthesized.

sections.label: Exposure system

paragraphs.text: Record the signal, frequency, modulation, field arrangement and source geometry. Establish whether reported quantities describe an external field, a whole-body absorbed metric or a localized tissue estimate. The animal’s position and the consistency of exposure across the enclosure can also affect interpretation.

NTP and Ramazzini are not equivalent versions of a person holding a phone or living near a tower. The studies’ mobile-communication signal names provide context; they do not make the complete experimental arrangement a direct measurement of ordinary user exposure.

sections.title: Identify what the experimental apparatus delivered

sections.label: Dosimetry

paragraphs.text: A field-strength value and an absorbed-power value should not be compared as though they were the same unit. A defensible programme comparison needs the dosimetry method, relevant tissue or whole-body region, animal size and uncertainties. A low external value does not by itself establish equivalent exposure to a human source.

Temperature and other conditions also require attention when interpreting an RF experiment. The method should explain how exposure conditions were monitored and how potential non-RF differences between groups were handled. Those details must come from the actual report rather than be reconstructed from a short abstract.

sections.title: Keep external fields and tissue dose distinct

sections.label: Schedule

paragraphs.text: Exposure starting before birth is a different protocol from exposure starting later. Hours per day, interruptions, duration and follow-up determine what period of the animal’s life is represented. A lifetime protocol may investigate a hazard without reproducing the time pattern of a particular human behavior.

Ramazzini’s selected record explicitly describes prenatal-to-natural-death exposure. The NTP record describes a controlled long-term whole-body programme. A detailed comparison should preserve their separate schedules and refrain from substituting a shared phrase such as “chronic RF” for those actual methods.

sections.title: Describe the life stage and time pattern

sections.label: Tumour assessment

paragraphs.text: NTP’s clearest selected judgment concerns malignant heart schwannomas in male rats, with different judgments by sex and tumour. Ramazzini reports a significant male-rat heart schwannoma increase at its highest exposure. Each finding should remain attached to those details when presented in a table.

Pathological definitions, blinding of assessment where documented, group numbers, survival and statistical methods need full-report appraisal. Small counts or survival differences can affect interpretation. A method record should leave undocumented details unknown rather than assume that a familiar programme name guarantees them.

sections.title: Read tissue, sex and survival with the result

sections.label: Programme comparison

paragraphs.text: The shared tumour focus can be relevant convergence, while protocol differences affect how strongly the studies corroborate a particular causal hypothesis. Comparison should explain both. Merely counting two positive papers hides which aspects were independently tested and which remain different.

The final translation to humans is a separate step involving tissue relevance, species and actual exposure. Neither this methods guide nor the experiment itself supplies a personal cancer-risk calculation. Use the animal outcome page for the bounded findings and the translation guide for the additional reasoning needed to connect them with human studies.

sections.title: Distinguish convergence from a duplicate experiment

takeaway: Compare field configuration, absorbed dose, schedule, sex, survival and pathology. The named tumour findings are interpretable only with those protocol details attached.
